deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page). A closed galvanic current S has elements (da,db,dc) at points (a,b,c); S denotes summation, i.e. a line integral, around the circuit. A magnet is a distribution of magnetic mass dm at points (x,y,z), with r^2=(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2+(z-c)^2. The Biot–Savart force on unit magnetic mass at (x,y,z) is taken as X = S[(y-b)dc-(z-c)db]/r^3, Y = S[(z-c)da-(x-a)dc]/r^3, Z = S[(x-a)db-(y-b)da]/r^3. Gauss wants the six resultants of the current's action on the rigid magnet: the three forces ∫X dm, ∫Y dm, ∫Z dm and the three moments ∫(zY-yZ)dm, ∫(xZ-zX)dm, ∫(yX-xY)dm. Note that ∫(yX-xY)dm is the negative of the modern (x×F)_z, which is only a sign convention. Notation (end of the previous page): V(a,b,c)=∫dm/r, ξ=∫(x-a)/r^3 dm, η=∫(y-b)/r^3 dm, ζ=∫(z-c)/r^3 dm. [Mine: ξ,η,ζ = ∂V/∂a, ∂V/∂b, ∂V/∂c, since ∂(1/r)/∂a=(x-a)/r^3.]

STEP 1 (prev. page). Pointwise, r^3(yX-xY) = [x(x-a)+y(y-b)]dc - (z-c)(x da+y db). Adding and subtracting z(z-c)dc gives [(x-a)x+(y-b)y+(z-c)z]dc - (z-c)(x da+y db+z dc).

STEP 2. Three substitutions:
- (x-a)x+(y-b)y+(z-c)z = r^2 + a(x-a)+b(y-b)+c(z-c).
- x da+y db+z dc = [(x-a)da+(y-b)db+(z-c)dc] + (a da+b db+c dc).
- (z-c) = z - c.

Integrating over dm and exchanging ∫ and S gives the first block on this page:
∫(yX-xY)dm = S V dc + S(ξa+ηb+ζc)dc - S ζ(a da+b db+c dc) + S c(ξ da+η db+ζ dc) - ∫ z S[(x-a)da+(y-b)db+(z-c)dc]/r^3 dm.
A first attempt '+S ξ a dc' is struck out and replaced by the full S(ξa+ηb+ζc)dc.

STEP 3. Collecting coefficients of ξ, η, ζ:
= S V dc + S{ξ(a dc+c da) + η(b dc+c db) + ζ(c dc - a da - b db)} - ∫ z S (d(1/r)/ds) ds dm.
The ζc dc terms combine as +1-1+1. Gauss recognises [(x-a)da+(y-b)db+(z-c)dc]/r^3 as the differential of 1/r along the circuit. Its S around a closed circuit therefore vanishes; this last step is left implicit.

STEP 4. 'Der zweite Theil auch =' S{(ξc-ζa)da + (ηc-ζb)db + (aξ+bη+cζ)dc}. This is a pure regrouping by da, db, dc.
[My completion of where this leads: second part + V dc = d(cV) + [(aξ+bη)dc - ζ(a da+b db)], because c(ξda+ηdb+ζdc)+V dc = d(cV) along the curve. Hence ∫(yX-xY)dm = S[(aξ+bη)dc - ζ(a da+b db)] = -S(a × (∇V×dl))_z.]

STEP 5 (bottom). ∫X dm = S(η dc - ζ db), i.e. (∫X,∫Y,∫Z)dm = S(∇V × dl). This follows directly from ∫X dm = S[dc∫(y-b)/r^3dm - db∫(z-c)/r^3dm]. It replaces the previous page's claim that ∫X dm = 0 'vermöge Voraussetzung'; the first attempt is struck out on this page.

Upshot (implicit). For a closed current, the total force and moment on the magnet equal those of elementary forces ∇V×dl applied at the current elements. These are, up to sign, the Ampère/Laplace forces of the magnet's field on the circuit. So action and reaction balance in total for closed circuits, even though the elementary Biot–Savart forces are not central. Everything is expressed through the magnet's potential V. This is preparatory work for the 'Grundformel' essay on the next page.
errors: No algebraic errors found; every displayed equality checks.
The vanishing of ∫ z S d(1/r) dm (closed circuit, exact differential) is not stated explicitly. Likewise the final reduction using c dV + V dc = d(cV) is not carried out on the page.
The sign before the last term is written over a blot in both blocks; the derivation requires a minus.
Internal correction of the previous page: '∫X dm = 0 vermöge Voraussetzung' is superseded here by ∫X dm = S(η dc - ζ db), which is nonzero in general.
Gauss's moment ∫(yX-xY)dm is the negative of the modern z-torque. This is a convention, not an error.

results.what: Total force of a closed current on a magnet expressed through the magnet's potential: ∫X dm = S(η dc - ζ db), i.e. F = ∮ ∇V × dl
results.modern_name: Force between a closed circuit and a magnet via the magnetic scalar potential (Biot–Savart/Laplace force, Newton's third law for closed circuits)
results.usually_credited_to: Biot–Savart and Laplace (1820); Ampère (1820s) on the equivalence and reciprocity of closed currents and magnets

results.what: Reduction of the moment ∫(yX-xY)dm to line integrals plus exact differentials (d(1/r), d(cV)) that vanish on a closed circuit, giving torque = moment of the forces ∇V×dl at the current elements
results.modern_name: Torque balance (angular-momentum reciprocity) between a closed current loop and a magnet
results.usually_credited_to: Ampère (Théorie mathématique, 1826); later treatments by Neumann and Weber

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine vector-calculus verification of action–reaction (force and torque) between a closed current and a magnet. Such results were known from Ampère and Laplace in the 1820s. Gauss's electrodynamic Nachlass, including the 'Grundformel' material, is partly published in Werke V. The page shows working style (potential V, gradient ξ,η,ζ, exact differentials around closed circuits) rather than a new result.
